name: MN-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Omar with large fundraising advantage
Republican challenger with minimal cash on hand
Prediction markets price near-certain Democratic win
model.rationale: Minneapolis-based MN-05 is one of the most Democratic districts in the country, and incumbent Ilhan Omar has out-raised her Republican opponent by roughly 8-to-1 while he holds under $50,000 on hand. Markets price her at about 99%, and no evidence suggests a competitive general election.
model.watch: A major scandal or unexpected third-party surge would be the only plausible route to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
This Minneapolis-area seat is among the most heavily Democratic districts in the nation, with a partisan lean of D+32. Incumbent Ilhan Omar is seeking another term after easily securing renomination. She has raised about $5.8 million and holds more than $1.3 million in cash, while Republican John Nagel has raised roughly $747,000 but reports only about $47,000 on hand, leaving him little to compete in the fall.

No independent or partisan groups are spending in the race, and prediction markets put Omar's chances at about 99%. With no public polling and no expert ratings, the forecast rests on the district's fundamentals, which point overwhelmingly to the incumbent. An independent candidate is on the ballot but lacks any visible campaign infrastructure. The race is rated Safe Democratic.
